summary: Best complementary all-payer candidate is the New Jersey State Inpatient Database (NJ SID), derived from NJDDCS hospital discharge abstracts. It can support facility-level inpatient case-mix comparison with the acquired Medicare 2024 DRGs if the relevant year, hospital identifiers, and usable fields are confirmed. Public aggregate access for a specific New Brunswick hospital/year was not established in this bounded review; do not treat this discovery as acquisition or as an all-payer estimate.

sources.title: NJ Hospital Discharge Data Collection System (NJDDCS)
sources.publisher: New Jersey Department of Health, Office of Health Care Quality Assessment
sources.geography: New Jersey hospitals; facility-level discharge records. Patient residence geography and availability of Middlesex County breakdowns require checking the current data dictionary and extract.
sources.period: Inpatient collection since 1981; hospital ED outpatient UB data added in 2004. The page identifies archived detailed documentation for discharge years 2008–2016; current release years were not established.
sources.grain: Underlying UB-derived records include hospital code, admission/discharge dates, services, charges, and insurer type. This is encounter-level source data, not a verified public aggregate table.
useful_fields: diagnosis and DRG fields are likely specified in the linked current data dictionary but were not verified in this review
observed_facts: NJDOH describes NJDDCS as utilization data derived from hospital Uniform Bill information.
The state page says non-confidential data are available through HCUP and that research data may also be obtained through Rutgers iPHD after IRB approval.
NJDOH advises users to verify findings against other data sources.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Inspect the current NJ HealthCAP Data Dictionary and Extract File Layout linked from the NJDOH page, then check HCUP availability and HCUPnet for a New Jersey SID slice for one named discharge year and RWJUH or Saint Peter’s. Record hospital identifier mapping, residence-versus-facility geography, exclusions, suppression, payer coverage, and whether diagnosis and DRG are separately available before acquisition. If no public aggregate query covers the target slice, treat row-level SID/iPHD access as a separate institutional pathway; do not accept terms or agreements as part of this task.
limitations: No direct data download URL or public query result for either target facility was verified.
The NJDOH page describes access routes, not a public all-payer table or evidence that a particular year is currently available.
Do not infer that Medicare-only DRG frequencies represent all-payer demand.
Hospital-level discharge records do not provide arrivals per hour unless a suitable time field and reporting coverage are confirmed.

sources.title: HCUP State Inpatient Databases (SID) Overview
sources.publisher: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality, Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project
sources.geography: Participating-state community hospitals; NJ file-composition documentation says New Jersey supplied general acute-care inpatient discharge abstracts. HCUP state data are for patients treated in hospitals in the state, not solely residents of that state.
sources.period: Calendar-year files based on discharge date, with a split 2015 file due to the ICD-9-CM to ICD-10-CM transition. Exact New Jersey years available through HCUP or HCUPnet were not verified.
sources.grain: SID is a census of inpatient discharge abstracts for participating state partners, with encounter-level records. Public HCUPnet tables may offer aggregate statistics for selected states/settings; availability of a relevant New Jersey facility-level table was not verified.
observed_facts: AHRQ describes SID as all-payer inpatient discharge records, including Medicare, Medicaid, private insurance, and uninsured patients.

AHRQ lists principal and secondary diagnoses, expected payment source, charges, length of stay, and admission/discharge status among common elements, while noting that elements such as hospital county identifiers vary.

SID records are calendar-year files based on discharge date; SID files are sold through the HCUP Central Distributor, with costs varying by state and year. HCUP users must complete DUA training and read and sign the State Database DUA.
sources.retrieval_next_step: First query HCUPnet for New Jersey inpatient statistics and confirm year, hospital or geography filters, diagnosis grouping, payer dimensions, and cell suppression before relying on any aggregate output. Separately check the HCUP state-year availability/catalog and New Jersey file composition for the selected slice. If a suitable public aggregate is unavailable, document the paid SID path and required DUA steps for an institution to evaluate; do not purchase or accept agreements here.
limitations: AHRQ's general SID description does not prove that public aggregate tables are available at the target facility level.
The New Jersey file-composition page notes hospitals may lack full-year reporting and does not establish whether special-unit stays are included.
Hospital county identifiers, patient residence county, revisit linkage, and individual elements vary by state and year.
SID measures inpatient stays, not all ED visits, observation, or hourly arrivals.

sources.title: HCUP Frequently Asked Questions: State databases and HCUPnet
sources.publisher: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality, Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project
sources.geography: Selected state statistics derived from SID and SEDD; public New Jersey query coverage and available geographies were not verified.
sources.period: State-specific years depend on database and state participation; exact New Jersey query years were not verified.
sources.grain: Aggregate tables/statistics from selected state inpatient and ED data; query-specific grain and suppression require inspection in HCUPnet.
useful_fields: ED statistics for visits not resulting in admission at the same facility
potential state and year dimensions, subject to HCUPnet availability
observed_facts: AHRQ says HCUPnet provides free statistics and tables from SID and SEDD for selected states and settings.
AHRQ says state databases are encounter-level all-payer sources and that HCUPnet availability varies by state and year.
SEDD covers ED encounters that do not result in admission to the same hospital; same-hospital ED admissions appear in SID.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Use HCUPnet to check whether New Jersey supports a one-year inpatient or ED query matching the chosen facility or county slice; save the query definition, output, dates, and any cell-suppression notes as a separate aggregate acquisition only after confirming the result's population and payer scope.
limitations: This is a query-tool discovery lead, not a confirmed New Jersey result or a direct download of the underlying records.
Public output may not identify RWJUH or Saint Peter’s individually and may not expose facility-by-diagnosis/DRG detail.
ED non-admit counts and inpatient stays are separate settings and should not be combined without an explicit workflow definition.

missing_inputs: Confirm exact discharge year(s) and the target facility identifiers for RWJUH CCN 310038 and Saint Peter’s CCN 310070 in the NJDDCS/HCUP hospital coding system.
Verify whether NJDOH or HCUPnet provides a public aggregate table at facility level and whether it reports suppression, payer coverage, and patient-residence geography.
Verify current NJ HealthCAP dictionary fields for complaint, diagnosis, DRG, arrival route, and available timestamps before mapping them to simulation variables.
No direct API/download URL for NJDDCS or a matching HCUPnet result was verified.
simulation_use: Candidate for annual all-payer inpatient case-mix comparison against the acquired Medicare 2024 DRGs, once year, facility mapping, payer coverage, diagnosis/DRG fields, and geography are confirmed. Use NJ SID or NJDDCS-derived outputs only for the setting and population they actually cover. Hour/day arrival distributions require a separately verified time-resolved source; neither annual inpatient discharge counts nor generic external benchmarks establish local arrivals per hour.
limitations: This is candidate research, not dataset acquisition; no records or aggregate outputs were downloaded.
The sources do not establish a locally usable estimate for Middlesex County or either named hospital.
HCUP access may involve purchase and data-use terms; institutional access may require IRB approval. No terms were accepted.
Only official pages were used; no applicability conclusion beyond the cited source descriptions is established.
